turns.content: Heating aniline with sulfuric acid gives a sulfonated product. Identify the major regioisomer and determine the substitution relationship relevant to later aromatic-proton equivalence.
After sodium bicarbonate treatment followed by sodium nitrite and HCl, identify product 2 and the functional-group changes that produced it.
Couple product 2 conventionally with 2-naphthol. Identify product 3 and determine the coupling position on the naphthol ring.
For the aniline-derived ring in product 3, use the substitution relationship established above to count its distinct nonexchangeable aromatic-proton environments.

For the naphthol-derived fused aromatic fragment, count the remaining aromatic hydrogens and their distinct environments. Then determine whether the product still has an exchangeable heteroatom-bound proton and how it contributes to the spectrum.
Make a fragment-by-fragment ledger that distinguishes the number of hydrogens from the number of distinct proton environments in each fragment.
Combine the fragment counts to obtain the total number of distinct nonexchangeable proton signals.
